title: Enterprise onboarding, support & QBR playbook
author: Priya Shah
summary: A single, operational playbook for Enterprise Onboarding covering integration checklists, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, support SLAs, health-check cadence and QBR templates. Intended for Customer Success, Support, Solutions Engineering and SRE handoffs.
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the standard playbook we use for enterprise customer onboarding, support escalation, integrations, known issues and quarterly business reviews (QBRs). It is designed to be step-by-step and prescriptive so teams (CS, Support, Solutions Engineering, SRE, and Product) can run consistent, low-risk onboarding and support operations for customers on Redwood Inference Dedicated and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments and O(>100k) monthly tokens on Hosted API when Sales/CS require an onboarding program.
- Covers initial tech integration (API, VPC/networking, auth), operational readiness, health checks, escalation process for incidents, and recurring QBR/health cadence.

Owners & Roles:
- Customer Success (CS): overall onboarding owner, QBR lead, customer communications.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): technical integration lead, validation of latency/cost expectations.
- Support (Tier 1 & Tier 2): triage, runbook execution, primary escalation contact.
- Eng SRE / Runtime Team: production incidents, capacity and kernel-level debugging.
- Security & Compliance: privacy/KMS/HSM and audit requirements.

Key SLOs & SLA targets (for onboarding window and ongoing support):
- Initial response to support ticket: P1 = 30 minutes, P2 = 2 hours, P3 = 1 business day.
- P1 incident target (system down / customer-facing outage): mitigation plan within 1 hour, 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated pools.
- Latency SLO for enterprise routes: p95 < 250ms for small (<512 tokens) generative requests (dependent on model variant).

Onboarding timeline & checklist (recommended 6-week default):
1. Kickoff (Week 0):
   - Owners: CS + SE
   - Deliverables: Kickoff deck, contacts, access list, NDA/contract confirmation, security questionnaire.
2. Environment & Access (Week 0-1):
   - Customer provides VPC peering details (if Private) or IP allowlist (if Dedicated).
   - SE to provision test API keys, configure roles, and add customer to console access.
   - Verify KMS/HSM integration (if required).
3. Integration & Testing (Week 1-3):
   - Run API smoke tests: auth, generation, streaming, embeddings, rate-limit behavior.
   - Validate sample workload (representative prompts) against latency and cost expectations.
   - Run KV/prefix caching validation and warm-up flow to ensure KV cache hits.
4. Load validation & Performance (Week 2-4):
   - Coordinate controlled traffic ramp (10%, 50%, 100%) with autoscaling policies observed.
   - Metrics to capture: token throughput, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, queue depth, error rates.
5. Cutover & Monitoring (Week 4-5):
   - Update DNS/routes, verify canary traffic (1-5%).
   - Finalize alerting and dashboards in Redwood Console.
6. QBR & Handoff (Week 5-6):
   - Deliver operational runbook, billing expectations, and failure/fallback plan.
   - Schedule first 30/60/90-day QBR cadence.

Integration checklist (API & infra) - minimum required items:
| Item | Owner | Validation |
|-----|-----|-----|
| API key issuance (test + prod) | SE | Successful auth + sample generation (curl) |
| Rate limits & quotas | CS + Billing | Confirm quotas in account and console alerts |
| VPC peering / IP allowlist | Customer + Eng Infra | Successful egress/ingress and traceroute to endpoint |
| KMS/HSM integration | Security | Keys accessible, encryption at rest validated |
| Model variant pinning & rollouts | Product + SE | Confirm model version and fallback policy configured |

Sample curl smoke test (place in SE playbook):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"Say hello in three languages","max_tokens":40}'

Escalation playbook (Incident severity and path):
- Severity definitions:
  - P1 (Critical): Total outage (all customers or single enterprise customer severely impacted), data loss, or major security incident.
  - P2 (High): Significant degradation for an enterprise customer (high error rate, major latency regression) with business impact.
  - P3 (Medium): Feature regressions, intermittent errors, non-critical performance issues.
  - P4 (Low): Minor UI/UX issues, documentation clarifications, or enhancement requests.

- Immediate actions for P1/P2:
  1) Triage in 15 minutes: Support acknowledges and opens incident channel (Slack #incident-<customer> and PagerDuty).
  2) Notify Execs & CS: CS to inform customer and provide ETA.
  3) Assign SRE and Runtime lead: collect logs (server logs, gateway logs, model runtime traces), capture p99/p95 metrics, and check recent deploys.
  4) If degradation is load-related: scale Dedicated pool or failover to alternate region/model variant per routing policy.
  5) Post-incident: root cause analysis within 72 hours and documented postmortem in confluence (link to incident template).

Escalation contacts (example):
- Support (Tier 1): support@redwood.ai, PagerDuty: Redwood-Support
- Support (Tier 2): lead-support@redwood.ai, PagerDuty: Redwood-Support-L2
- SRE / Runtime on-call: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai, PagerDuty: Redwood-Runtime
- CS escalation: enterprise-cs@redwood.ai (CS leads: Priya Shah / Evan Martinez)

Known issues & workarounds (living list - update when triaged):
| ID | Symptom | Impact | Workaround | Owner |
|----|---------|--------|-----------|-------|
| KI-2025-001 | Occasional p95 spikes for long-context gen (>2048 tokens) | Intermittent latency regression for customers using long prompts | Suggest prefix caching and reduce context window; if persistent, set model variant to quantized-large for longer sequences | Runtime Team |
| KI-2025-014 | Streaming disconnects on slow mobile networks | Partial delivery of tokens; customers see truncated responses | Enable short polling fallback in client and lower stream chunk size; increase stream keepalive timeout | Support |
| KI-2026-003 | Embeddings 429s under sudden ramp | Higher error rate for bulk-embedding jobs | Implement client-side exponential backoff, shard jobs across API keys, and request rate-limit increase via CS | SE / Support |

Support process & ticket lifecycle:
- Ticket intake: Support (Tier 1) triages inbound issues using the triage checklist and assigns priority.
- Triage checklist: reproduce issue, gather logs (request ID, model, route, sample payload), capture timestamps & p95/p99 latency windows, check for recent deploys.
- Routing:
  - Product bugs -> Product/Runtime triage board (label: product-bug).
  - Security -> Security channel and SSO with immediate incident review.
  - Capacity / scaling -> SRE with capacity playbook.
- SLAs for updates: P1 = update every 30 minutes until mitigated; P2 = update every 2 hours; P3/P4 = update every business day.

Health checks and QBR materials (what to measure and a sample agenda):
- Operational metrics to include in health report:
  - Monthly active routes, top-10 customer routes by token volume, token throughput (total tokens/day), p50/p95/p99 latency by route, error rates by route (5xx/4xx), Dedicated pool GPU utilization and queue depth, cache hit ratio (prefix/KV).
  - Cost and efficiency: tokens per GPU-hour, average tokens per request, batching efficiency.
  - Quality signals: sample prompt-set pass rate, hallucination/regression alerts (from Redwood Optimize).

- QBR cadence & sample agenda (30-60 mins):
  1) Intro & agenda (5 mins)
  2) Business outcomes & usage trends (10 mins)
  3) Operational health (metrics + incidents since last QBR) (10 mins)
  4) Cost & optimization opportunities (batching, quantization, routing) (10 mins)
  5) Roadmap & upcoming changes (product & infra) (10 mins)
  6) Action items & next steps (5 mins)

QBR slide template (high level):
- Cover slide (contacts, period)
- Executive summary (usage & health)
- Ops metrics dashboard (latency, errors, GPU utilization)
- Cost breakdown & optimization recommendations
- Risk & mitigations (planned upgrades, deprecations)
- Action items & owners

Handoffs & runbooks:
- Handoff from SE to Support: must include validated sample payloads, identified canary routes, test API keys, and expected SLOs. Use handoff checklist: Handoff Checklist (SE -> Support) -> attach to customer account in CRM.
- Runbooks: maintain runbooks for common classes of incidents (auth failures, model OOM, routing fallback). Each runbook must include: symptoms, quick triage steps, mitigation (temp workaround), permanent fix timeline, and owner.

Change management during onboarding:
- Any infra or runtime config changes that affect enterprise customers require:
  1) Change ticket in Jira with risk assessment.
  2) 72-hour notice to CS + customer if change affects SLA or routing.
  3) Canary rollout with rollback plan and health-check gating.

Appendix / Links:
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template
- Runtime performance dashboard: Redwood Console -> Dashboards -> Enterprise Onboarding
- Integration API reference: https://docs.redwood.ai/api
- Support SLAs & contacts: internal://support/contacts

Maintenance notes:
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly by CS and Runtime teams.
- Update known-issues table immediately after triage and add regression tickets to the Runtime backlog.
